title: acme-data, mapped
subtitle: Where Acme Foods' sales data comes from, which layers it passes, who reads it, who owns it and where personal data goes. Read from the code only: no database was contacted.

verdict.text: This is Acme Foods' nightly sales warehouse: six ERP tables pass through dbt staging into marts, T-SQL procedures and a Spark notebook write beside them, and nothing anywhere masks personal data. Look first at `exports/marketing_contacts.sql:6`, which sends national ID numbers to the marketing tool every month, then at the promotion join in `models/marts/fct_sales.sql:33`, which inflates every sales figure downstream.

flows.title: Sales: from an ERP order to the figure a manager sees

steps.text: `erp.orders` and `erp.order_lines` become staging views with typed dates and prices (`models/staging/stg_orders.sql:6`, `models/staging/stg_order_lines.sql:3`). In the sample CSVs, 300 of 1,500 dates are written `dd.mm.yyyy` and 120 of 3,000 prices use a decimal comma. The casts at `stg_orders.sql:16` and `stg_order_lines.sql:14` are plain, so whether those values convert, fail or swap day and month depends on the engine. [med]

Lines are joined to their order and cancelled orders are dropped (`models/intermediate/int_order_lines.sql:28-29`). Returned orders stay in. The model is ephemeral, so this logic is compiled into `fct_sales` and no table exists. [high]
The sales fact reads the joined lines (`models/marts/fct_sales.sql:6`). `models/marts/schema.yml:32` documents one row per order line, and no test checks it. [high]

The discount join matches on `product_id` alone, with no date condition (`models/marts/fct_sales.sql:33`, added in commit 81c7521 on 2026-08-06). [high] On the sample data, 2,787 lines become 3,323 rows (+19%) and 730 lines get a discount from a promotion that was not running. Net sales come to 745,281 against 686,210 with the dates respected (+8.6%), which is higher even than the 689,761 before any discount.

`dw.load_daily_sales` sums one day per store and product and inserts it (`warehouse/procs/load_daily_sales.sql:15-22`). Nothing deletes first, so running a date twice doubles that date, and fixing the promotion join will not correct days already loaded. `customer_id` is grouped away here. [high]

The store report keeps only `completed` orders by joining back to `staging.stg_orders` (`reports/store_performance.sql:8-11`). Returned orders are in `dw.fct_daily_sales` but not here, a 3.1% gap in net sales on the sample. [high]

`dw.export_by_region` reads the daily table through a statement built as a string, with the form's region name pasted in (`warehouse/procs/export_by_region.sql:10,12`). The inventory script cannot see this read. [high]
A comment says this table feeds the Power BI dataset (`warehouse/ddl/fct_daily_sales.sql:1`). Nothing in the repo confirms it, see Open questions.

flows.title: Customer details: from the ERP to the marketing tool

steps.text: All nine columns pass through unchanged, including `national_id` and `birth_date` (`models/staging/stg_customers.sql:3,10-18`). [high]

The same nine columns, rebuilt as a table every night (`models/marts/dim_customer.sql:5,12-20`). The `unique` test on `customer_id` (`models/marts/schema.yml:9`) would fail on the sample, which has 406 rows for 400 ids, and staging tests only `not_null`. [high]
Gold and silver customers are selected (`exports/marketing_contacts.sql:9-10`). Line 6 lists `national_id` on the same line as `email`, and a mailing has no use for it. [high]
Marketing loads the result into its campaign tool by hand, for the monthly mailing (`exports/marketing_contacts.sql:1`). The repo does not name the tool, see Open questions.
`dim_product` is the copy that `fct_sales` and the notebook use (`models/marts/dim_product.sql:3`). [high]

`dw.merge_dim_product` keeps a second copy with no reader in this repo (`warehouse/procs/merge_dim_product.sql:7-17`). The MERGE has no `WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE`, so a product removed from the ERP stays here and disappears from `dim_product`. [high]

The notebook reads `erp.stock_levels` and a monthly adjustments table whose name it builds at run time (`notebooks/stock_snapshot.ipynb` cell 3, lines 1 and 4). Neither is declared in dbt, and staging is skipped. [high]
It adds `region` from `dim_store`, named without a schema (cell 3, line 2), so the table it gets depends on Spark's current database. I assumed `marts.dim_store`. [med]

`snapshot_date` is fixed at `2026-09-30` (cell 2, line 1) and the write overwrites the table (cell 4, line 12), so as committed every 06:00 run produces the same date. [high] The first cell names the ordering team as the reader, see Open questions.

blocks.title: Layers, and what does not fit
items: `erp` to `staging` (views) to `intermediate` (ephemeral) to `marts` (tables): this is the dbt line (`dbt_project.yml:15-23`). [high]
`dw` is not a step after marts. `dw.fct_daily_sales` reads `marts.fct_sales`, but `dw.dim_product` reads staging directly, and both are loaded by T-SQL procedures outside dbt. [high]
`marts.stock_snapshot` sits in the marts schema but Spark writes it straight from `erp`, outside dbt and past staging. [high]
`reports/store_performance.sql:10` reads `staging.stg_orders` directly, past marts. `dw.export_by_region` mixes `dw` and `marts`. [high]

blocks.title: When it runs (from the README and comments, the scheduler is not in this repo)
items: Every night, 02:00
`dbt run`, then `dw.merge_dim_product`, then `dw.load_daily_sales` for yesterday (`README.md:20-24`)
Every day, 06:00
Spark job: the stock snapshot notebook (`README.md:26`)
Every Monday
Store performance report (`reports/store_performance.sql:1`)
Monthly
Marketing contact list (`exports/marketing_contacts.sql:1`)
On request
`dw.export_by_region`, from the request form (`README.md:26`, `warehouse/procs/export_by_region.sql:1`)

blocks.title: What reading the code changed
blocks.text:
The inventory script found 24 links between tables. I read each one in the code and added three it could not see: the two reads inside the dynamic SQL at `warehouse/procs/export_by_region.sql:10`, and the monthly table at notebook cell 3, line 4. The script found no cycles and neither did I. [high]

The five links into people and outside tools come from comments, so they say what someone intended and not what runs.

Three names look like tables but are not read by any statement: `old_orders_backup` (`models/staging/stg_orders.sql:5`) and `retired_table` (`warehouse/procs/load_daily_sales.sql:16`) are comments, and `finance_ledger` (`reports/store_performance.sql:7`) is a footnote string. [high]

sections.title: Tables
sections.intro: Owner is the git author of the file. The repo has 10 commits from two people between 2026-06-09 and 2026-10-20, and every SQL file was committed once except `fct_sales.sql`, committed twice. The last change to SQL was on 2026-09-24. The last three rows are the consumers with code here, not tables.

rows: dw.export_by_region; Power BI, per a comment

sections.title: Dynamic SQL
sections.intro: A script cannot read these, so I opened each one.

rows: A `SELECT` on `dw.fct_daily_sales` joined to `marts.dim_store`, filtered by region. [high]
`@region`, pasted between quotes, from the request form according to the comment on line 1. [high]

As intended, those two tables. As written, a value containing a quote can end the string and run its own statement, and 60 characters is enough for that. It runs with the rights of the login behind the form, which could include reading `marts.dim_customer`. The repo holds no `GRANT` or `EXECUTE AS`, so those rights are not known. [med]
`month_suffix` is derived from `snapshot_date`, fixed in cell 2. No outside input in the code. [high]
As committed, only `erp.stock_adjustments_2026_09`. A changed date reaches any `erp.stock_adjustments_YYYY_MM`, and that is the whole of its range. [high]

sections.title: Nobody reads these
sections.intro: The script listed four tables with no reader in this repo. After reading the code, two are open questions and two have a reader. None of this says a table is safe to remove: a tool outside this repo may read it.

rows: No reader here. Merged every night by `dw.merge_dim_product`, while `fct_sales` and the notebook use the dbt `dim_product`. [high]
Vesna Lipovac: what was it for, and does Power BI read it?
No reader here. Rebuilt on every `dbt run`. Its commit a2fd916 calls it the campaign mart for the summer review, so it may have been a one-off. [med]
Vesna Lipovac: is the summer review over?
**Has a reader.** `dw.export_by_region` reads it inside dynamic SQL (`warehouse/procs/export_by_region.sql:10`), and the DDL comment names the Power BI dataset. [high]
No reader in code, but the notebook says it is written for the ordering team (cell 1). [high]
Marko Javor: how does the ordering team read it?

sections.title: Where personal data goes
sections.intro: A search of the whole repo for masking, hashing, encryption, `GRANT`, `EXECUTE AS`, retention and erasure finds nothing. [high]

blocks.text: Personal data is masked nowhere. `national_id` travels in clear from `erp.customers` to Marketing's campaign tool, and `exports/marketing_contacts.sql:6` is the line that sends it out. [high]

blocks.title: Column by column
rows: campaign tool, and on every row of `fct_sales`

items.title: Identity and contact
items.text: `erp.customers`, `stg_customers`, `dim_customer`, `marketing_contacts`, then by hand to the campaign tool. No step removes or masks a column except that the export leaves out phone and birth date. [high]

items.title: Purchase history
items.text: `erp.orders.customer_id` goes through `stg_orders` and `int_order_lines` into `fct_sales`, where each sale can be joined back to `dim_customer`. It stops there: `dw.load_daily_sales` groups it away and the store report does not select it. [high]

items.title: A copy on disk
items.text: `data/customers.csv` has the same personal columns and 406 rows. It is ignored by git, so it exists only in working copies. I read its header and its `customer_id` column, not the values.

blocks.title: What the reach view does and does not show
blocks.text:
The reach view follows the links in the code. It starts the purchase-history path at `int_order_lines` because `stg_orders` also feeds the store report, which takes only `order_id` and `status` from it. It stops at `fct_sales` because no reader selects `customer_id` from there, and that is not masking: anyone who can read `fct_sales` can make the join.

It does not draw the risk at `dw.export_by_region`. No code path carries customer data there, but a crafted region name could read `marts.dim_customer` if the login allows it. See Dynamic SQL.

sections.title: Open questions
sections.intro: These cannot be answered from the repository. Who to ask comes from git, and both people may have moved on.

blocks.title: To ask
items: **Marketing's campaign tool.** Which tool is it, who holds the files and why does it receive `national_id`? What is the legal basis for that? Ask Vesna Lipovac and Marketing.
**The request form behind `dw.export_by_region`.** Who can submit it, and under which database login does it run? That login sets what a crafted region name can reach.
**Which sales figure is official?** The store report counts `completed` orders. `dw.fct_daily_sales`, Power BI and the regional export count everything not cancelled.

**Which engine does dbt run on?** `dbt_project.yml:5` names the profile `acme_dw` and no `profiles.yml` is here. The procedures are T-SQL and read dbt's tables directly, yet `models/intermediate/int_order_lines.sql:26` uses `EXTRACT`, which I do not expect SQL Server to accept. [med] The column it makes, `order_year`, is used nowhere.

**Do the schema names line up?** dbt by default names a custom schema `<target>_marts` [med], and the repo has no macro to change that, yet the procedures and reports read `marts.…` and `staging.…`. Check what the database actually contains.
**How do Spark and T-SQL see the same tables?** The notebook reads `marts.dim_product` and `erp.stock_levels` through Spark, and the procedures read `[marts]` through T-SQL.
**Who makes the nightly ERP copy, and does it finish before 02:00?** `models/staging/schema.yml:5` only says it exists. Nothing in this repo loads `erp.*`, and the scheduler is not here either.
**The Power BI dataset.** Which tables does it read, and who owns it? Only `warehouse/ddl/fct_daily_sales.sql:1` mentions it.
**The stock job.** Does the 06:00 job override `snapshot_date`, and how does the ordering team read the result? Ask Marko Javor. The notebook has no parameter cell.
**The Monday report.** Who runs `reports/store_performance.sql`, and how does it reach the regional managers?
**Is `data/customers.csv` real customer data?** If it is, it should not be sitting in working copies.
**Are Vesna Lipovac and Marko Javor still reachable?** They are the only two authors in the history.

blocks.title: What I assumed
items: Schedules and consumers named in the README and in comments are true. Nothing in this repo runs them or confirms them.
`marts.x` and `staging.x` in T-SQL are the tables dbt builds from the model of the same name.
`dim_store` in the notebook is `marts.dim_store`.
The git author of a file stands in for its owner.

The CSVs in `data/` behave like the ERP tables. Every figure marked as sample comes from them, not from production. Dates written `dd.mm.yyyy` are read day first: 175 of those 300 can only be read that way.
`docs/briefs/` holds plans for a later platform and for a sister company, so nothing in those files is on this map.
The dbt schema naming and the `EXTRACT` point come from general knowledge. I could not open the documentation in this session.
